Hi Sophie — glad to help. Below is a concise Q&A you can drop into procurement. I attached a CSV of active subprocessors and a simple data-trajectory diagram (see attachments).

Q: Where is request/response processing performed for a standard hosted PoC?
A: By default, request ingestion, tokenization, and model inference occur in our Redwood-hosted cluster in AWS us-west-2 (Oregon). Temporary KV cache and ephemeral model contexts are also kept in that region. Any short-lived telemetry used for routing/metrics is retained in US regions.

Q: Which subprocessors are involved and where are they located?
A: Current subprocessors (abridged):
- AWS (us-west-2) — primary compute & ephemeral storage — United States
- CloudFront / CDN (global) — edge caching only; no persistent customer payload storage
- Sentry (US) — telemetry/alerts (PII redaction in place)
- PagerDuty (US) — incident management
- Segment (US) — usage analytics (can be disabled for customers)
(Full CSV attached: redwood-subprocessors-2026.csv)

Q: Is any processing done outside the US by default?
A: No. For our hosted PoC, persistent and inference processing stays in us-west-2. Certain CDN edge hops may route through carrier networks internationally for low-level transport (no persistent storage), and telemetry is routed to US-based logging services. If a customer requires EU or APAC processing we offer region-specific hosting (EU: eu-west-1/eu-central-1; APAC: ap-northeast-1) via Dedicated or Private deployments.

Q: Do we do cross-border transfers and what safeguards exist?
A: Cross-border transfer only occurs when a customer explicitly selects a region outside the US or when carrier network hops occur (transit). For our standard hosted PoC (US), there is no intentional cross-border storage. For customers using EU regions, we support SCCs where applicable and maintain a subprocessor matrix plus SOC 2+ audit evidence on request.

Q: How do deletion and retention work for PoC data?
A: PoC data lifecycle:
- Short-term cache: ephemeral (seconds to minutes) to optimize latency; automatically evicted.
- Inference logs/metrics: default TTL 30 days; can be shortened or disabled for PoCs on request.
- Customer-requested deletion: we run a wipe across the involved stores and confirm completion within 72 hours for hosted PoCs (48 hours typical). Deletion confirmation includes a signed statement and a job ID.

Q: Proof for procurement: what artifacts can we provide?
A: We can provide: subprocessor CSV, data-trajectory diagram (attached), SOC 2 Type II report redaction summary, SCC statement draft, and a retention/deletion exhibit. Links: HubSpot record and a Drive folder are included below.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-2026.csv, data-trajectory-diagram-2026.png

Hi Sophie — quick answers from ops: 
- Deletion SLA scope: our 72-hour confirmation covers all customer-associated data for the PoC environment, including inputs/outputs and inference logs/metrics that are stored beyond ephemeral caches. Short-lived telemetry that is not persisted (ephemeral caches) are evicted automatically and are not subject to manual wipe. When we run a manual wipe we execute coordinated jobs across object stores, logs indexers, and our internal cache invalidation service and provide a job ID with the confirmation.
- CDN edge caching: by default we do not configure persistent customer payload caching at CDN edge origins for PoCs. Edge is used only for static assets and routing; any request/response bodies are streamed through without persistent edge persistence.

Attached is a short retention/deletion exhibit you can attach to procurement (retention-deletion-exhibit.pdf). If procurement needs a signed exhibit we can set a mutual signature workflow — happy to do that once we have the SOW step completed.

Best,
Jordan Blake
